questions: Should the function modify the input list 'l' in-place (e.g., shuffle it) before using it, or work on a copy to avoid side effects?
If the input list has fewer than three elements, what should happen when moving the first three to the end? Should it wrap around, produce an error, or just return the array unchanged?
Is the shuffling step required even for custom input lists, or only when the default list is used?
Should the output array always be of string dtype (since ELEMENTS are strings), or should it preserve the numeric/non-numeric type of the input list?
What should be the order of the first three elements after moving to the end? Should they maintain their original order relative to each other, or be reversed/otherwise rearranged?
If the input list contains duplicate values, does shuffling treat them as distinct, and does moving elements depend on positions only?
Should the function set a random seed internally for reproducibility, or rely on external seeding?
Is the output array required to be a new numpy array, or can it be a view/slice of the original array?
